subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: How should managed Memory Dreaming cron surface a run where the outer agent turn succeeds but one or more workspaces fail or produce no durable Dreaming output?
rationale: Current code can log failed workspace work inside memory-core while cron records the outer run status; choosing whether that becomes cron error, skipped/degraded diagnostics, or doctor-only visibility is a product and operations contract decision.

options.title: Surface degraded Dreaming status
options.body: Record structured Dreaming run diagnostics that cron list/doctor can show as degraded or failed when workspace failure counts are nonzero or durable output is stale, without changing the silent delivery mode.

options.title: Keep cron ok and require live repro
options.body: Treat the SQLite migration and recent doctor warnings as sufficient for now, and only change status semantics after a fresh v2026.6.11/current-main reproduction proves a remaining silent no-op.

options.title: Close as legacy-only after maintainer signoff
options.body: Close this issue if maintainers decide the remaining status-visibility concern should be handled only by broader cron diagnostics or a new narrower report.

recommendation.title: Surface degraded Dreaming status
recommendation.body: Record structured Dreaming run diagnostics that cron list/doctor can show as degraded or failed when workspace failure counts are nonzero or durable output is stale, without changing the silent delivery mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite-state repair and prior Dreaming alignment work make this the strongest available owner for deciding whether the remaining behavior belongs in memory-core, cron, or doctor diagnostics.
